practiceReport.name: Alex Highsmith
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Trench/box position (LB) — historically higher active rate through braced upper-body & ankle soreness (81% baseline).
practiceReport.beatComment: Highsmith recorded a pair of sacks across just six snaps before he was forced out in the first quarter of Sunday's 19-16 loss to the Eagles due to the ankle injury. Per Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com, the Steelers' initial belief is that Highsmith's ankle injury isn't serious, but the edge rusher will nonetheless have difficulty getting clearance to play on a short week. If healthy, Nick Herbig (hip/ribs) -- who was inactive for Week 11 -- will be the most likely candidate to start in place of Highsmith on Friday.

practiceReport.name: Ben Skowronek
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Perimeter speed/cut position (WR) — requires full deceleration/burst clearance on lower-body tags (76% Questionable baseline).
factors: Beat trend: trending downward / setback caution ahead of game
practiceReport.beatComment: The 29-year-old appears to have suffered a setback with his calf injury, as he opened Week 12 as a non-participant in practice Tuesday. Skowronek missed the Steelers' last three games due to the same injury. He will likely need to upgrade his practice status for a chance to play Friday against the Broncos.

practiceReport.name: DeShon Elliott
practiceReport.archetypeNote: Standard NFL positional availability baseline (78% Questionable conversion).
factors: Mid-week downgrade (Wed FP -> Thu LP); monitoring Friday clearance
practiceReport.beatComment: Elliott was cleared to return from a one-game absence due to a knee injury to play against the Eagles in Week 11, when he played 22 snaps (14 on defense, eight on special teams) while not showing up in the box score otherwise. Even if he's cleared to play Friday against the Broncos, Elliott would likely operate in a rotational role in the secondary behind Jalen Ramsey, Jaquan Brisker and Robert Spears-Jennings.

practiceReport.beatComment: Dunker has put together four consecutive full sessions since being designated to return from injured reserve this past Wednesday. The rookie third-rounder is in the final stages of his recovery from an MCL sprain that he sustained in September. Dunker would need to be activated from IR in order to be available for Friday's game against the Broncos.

practiceReport.beatComment: Herbig upgraded his DNP practice status from last week to limited participation Tuesday. The 25-year-old missed Week 11 due to a hip injury. He has two more practice sessions to increase his chances of playing Friday against the Broncos.

practiceReport.archetypeNote: Veteran starter profile (7th NFL season, 78% snap share) — elevated Questionable active conversion (84%) & Wednesday maintenance tolerance.

practiceReport.beatComment: Pittman also logged a full participation listing one day before, but the Steelers held a walkthrough practice Tuesday, so Wednesday's session is more relevant with regard to the WR's availability for Friday's game against the Broncos. If Pittman -- who last saw game action in Week 4 -- is activated to face Denver, he'll be catching passing in Week 12 from Mason Rudolph, with the Steelers slated to let veteran signal-calller Aaron Rodgers go.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Jack Driscoll
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Driscoll will now need to miss at least four games of the regular season on injured reserve before he is eligible to return to the Steelers' active roster. The offensive tackle is dealing with an unknown issue, and it is unclear if he will need more than the minimum required time to recover.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Sebastian Joseph-Day
irAndReserveTracker.byeWeekNote: Week 9 Bye excluded from NFL 4-game minimum count
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: Joseph-Day is dealing with an apparent triceps injury, and he will now be forced to miss at least four contests while recovering. In his absence, Gabriel Rubio and Kevin Jobity are both candidates to see an increase in workload on Pittsburgh's defensive line.

irAndReserveTracker.name: Mason McCormick
irAndReserveTracker.beatNote: McCormick dislocated his ankle during the Steelers' 38-18 loss to the Bengals on Sunday. The good news for the third-year pro is that he avoided a fracture and does not require surgery, so there's a chance he could return for the Steelers should the team qualify for the playoffs, per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network. Brock Hoffman figures to start at left guard in McCormick's stead.
